## touch-browser v1.0.0

V1 product release for the local single-operator Touch Browser workflow.

### Added

- Added explicit `prompt-injection-attempt` policy signals for hostile pages, fake system/developer instructions, credential exfiltration prompts, and hidden instruction fixtures.
- Added prompt-injection guard coverage to the release readiness gate.

### Changed

- Promoted the internal readiness artifact to `product-ready` only when all tracked release gates pass.
- Tightened adversarial benchmark readiness so unsafe auto-answer counts must stay at zero and review capture must be complete.
- Bumped Rust workspace, MCP package metadata, MCP server descriptors, bridge metadata, workflow client metadata, Glama install pin, and standalone lifecycle expectations to `1.0.0`.
- Aligned the AWS Lambda adversarial sample with the current official overview page wording.

### Release Notes

- GitHub standalone release assets are the release channel for this tag.
- npm publishing is intentionally not part of this tag because npm authentication is unavailable in this environment; Glama/npm publication is handled separately by the maintainer.

### Verified

- Local fixture generation passed for safety metrics, adversarial benchmark, and release readiness.
- Local quality CI gate passed.
- Local public-web release gate passed.
- Local proof gate passed after regenerating proof artifacts.
- Local MCP package check passed.
- Local `v1.0.0` standalone bundle build and installed smoke passed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/nangman-infra/touch-browser/compare/v0.7.1...v1.0.0
